decisions.rationale: Quality is improving and multiples are still below their own history, so the thesis has not broken. But the mispricing that justified entry has largely closed: the reverse DCF now needs above-trend growth and the DCF range sits below the price. Conviction falls to 3. Hold the existing position; no add, and no forced sale while fundamentals keep improving.

Reaching base fair value has not completed the thesis. Multiples remain below their own 5-year floor and below peers, returns are rising and Q3 service and modernization growth was solid. Stalled margins, rising leverage and a stretched short-term chart rule out an ADD. No trigger has fired, so the existing size is kept.

Thesis intact and every trigger clear; multiples remain at the bottom of their own range. But the base fair value gap has narrowed and the bear value sits well below the price, so the skew no longer justifies adding ahead of Nov 19 results. Keep the existing size; no trim warranted while quality keeps rising.

Margins, cash conversion and net cash are intact and valuation is below every 5y low, so the thesis holds at conviction 4 and the position stays at its conviction size. The guidance cut, rival discounting and falling ROIC leave growth unresolved, so there is no case for conviction 5 or an ADD. Macro is context only.

Thesis intact: Q3 beat, margins and cash still rising, valuation still below own-history floors. Newly disclosed AI risk, a Core segment growing only slowly, partly price-led bookings and the class action keep conviction at 4, not 5, so no ADD. The position is already around its conviction size; hold it.

The quality figures reflect the gold price more than a verified moat. The history has no downturn, fair value is unavailable, and the multiples are a premium to peers, so there is no margin of safety. Results on Nov 13 add event risk. Good but not compelling at conviction 2: AVOID, no position.

Cheap on current cash flow, but current cash flow is probably peak: FCF far exceeds earnings, margins are cyclical, backlog is unresearched and results are days away after an unexplained sell-off. Good but not compelling, so conviction is 3 and the decision is AVOID. Macro is context only.

Strong current cash flow and a clean balance sheet, but margins track the gold price, there is no verifiable cost or reserve edge, dilution continues, and the macro overlay tilts toward bear after a sharp rally. The skew is roughly balanced, not compelling: AVOID. Price is not the main obstacle, so no entry price.

Strong balance sheet and FCF yield, but returns track the oil price, TTM earnings are above FY2024-25 levels, the stock has already doubled and the mechanical bear value sits below the price with modest upside to base. Good but not compelling: AVOID, with an entry price at base fair value less the margin of safety.

Quality and cheapness against its own history are real. But the base upside is modest, the EV/EBITDA method and bear value sit below the price, the margin may be near a peak, and guidance is for a softer net margin. Q3 results are due in three days, and primary-source research is thin. Good but not compelling, so AVOID; the entry price is set instead.

Quality and backlog are strong and multiples are low, but earnings look cyclical-peak, the cause of the six-month collapse is unknown, base fair value sits well below the price and volatility is extreme. Good but not compelling: conviction 3, so AVOID; re-research on a further de-rating toward the margin-of-safety entry.

Quality and valuation are attractive, but I can't tell whether the doubled operating margin is structural. Segment mix and the Q2 results are unread, the mechanical bear value is below the price and FCF conversion is lumpy. Good but not compelling: conviction 3, AVOID, with an entry price at base fair value less the margin of safety.

The business is cheap and highly cash-generative, but the reverse DCF roughly matches guided Q4 revenue, so the edge depends on an unproven Tinder revenue turnaround. A 2027 fee headwind, platform risk, leverage and a far-lower bear value make it good but not compelling. Conviction 3: AVOID.

Quality trend and cash conversion are real, but the discount is sector-wide, the DCF likely overstates a family-controlled holdco, the segment mix and leverage are unverified from primary sources, and results are due Nov 11, 2026. Good but not compelling: conviction 3, AVOID; cash is acceptable.

The credible P/B + ROE value is only modestly above the price and its bear is below it; the higher blended value rests on a bank FCFE DCF. Dilution, a new part-stock acquisition, non-recurring Q3 gains and a bear-leaning macro tilt make this good but not compelling. Cash is preferable.

The setup is invalid: the jump is a cash bid, not a results beat. The honest target is the offer, so reward:risk is far below 2:1 against the volatility stop, and a deal break would gap through the stop. Closing is also beyond the drift time limit. No position.

The setup's edge has gone: the close is under the reaction-day low, so the volatility stop sits inside one day's noise and the 2:1 ratio is meaningless. Valuation far above own history and fair value adds gap risk. Business quality is excellent but conviction rates the trade, not the company; cash is preferable.

The beat is real, but the volatility-based stop is only about 0.4 ATR below the close in a high-beta, high-VIX tape, so a noise stop-out is likely; the target barely clears the 108.39 swing high and part of the jump was a broker pick, not results. Reward:risk holds on paper only. Not compelling; cash is fine.

The setup is real, but the wide reaction-day stop forces a target the evidence only reaches on the bull DCF case, with RSI 76.5 and a 100.8x EV/EBITDA adding gap risk. Reward:risk passes on paper but not on probability. That makes this good, not compelling, so it is an AVOID and cash is the outcome. Macro is context only.

The honest target is the 437.79 swing high, about 1:1 against the ATR stop at 343.37. Reaching 486.92 needs a break above the 200-day and the August high inside 8 weeks, with RSI 76.3, beta 2.50 and a risk-off tape. The edge is unclear, so we avoid and hold cash.

Post-earnings drift needs a real beat; the Q3 release came six days earlier with falling margins and negative FCF. The volatility stop at 58.77 forces a 77.46 target that no evidence supports (above the 76.20 52-week high and 68.31 bull fair value). Below 2:1 on an honest target, so AVOID.

No evidenced earnings beat (TTM margins collapsed to losses), a barely-qualifying reaction, and a minimum target above the 52-week high make the reward:risk unsupported; extreme EV/Sales and P/B add gap risk. Conviction 2: AVOID, no position.

The volatility stop at 316.65 implies a 2:1 target of 426.52, well beyond the 371.18 52-week high, with price +18.3% above the 50-day and above bull fair value. The honest target cannot reach 2:1, so per owner rules this is an AVOID. Macro is context only.

The drift edge is weak: no beat, guidance only affirmed, RSI 82.4 and a 50-day still below the 200-day. The mechanical 2:1 target sits above the 52-week high, so reward:risk depends on a full retracement within eight weeks. Volume and hold are real, but good-not-compelling is an AVOID; macro is context only.

The beat is real but the trade fails: the honest target is the 52-week high of 48.20, short of the 2:1 level of 49.03 against a volatility stop at 38.83. RSI of 87.9 and a P/E above its 5y maximum add gap risk. No position; cash is acceptable.
